quarterly_data.signal: 10-K fiscal 2026 (year ended March 31, 2026) results: net sales were $4,713.1 million, up 7.1% from $4,401.6 million, with net sales up in all product lines and all geographies as customers worked down excess inventory and new design wins entered production. By segment, semiconductor products were $4,549.3 million and technology licensing $163.8 million (+24.9% per XBRL); by product line, mixed-signal microcontrollers were $2,355.4 million (50.0%), analog $1,329.0 million (28.2%) and other $1,028.7 million (21.8%). Gross margin was 57.7% versus 56.1%; inventory fell to $1.04 billion (185 days) from $1.29 billion (251 days). Management: 'we are now in a significant revenue growth mode'.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 net sales $4,713.1 million (+7.1%); semiconductor products $4,549.3 million; licensing $163.8 million; MCU $2,355.4 million, analog $1,329.0 million; gross margin 57.7%; inventory 185 days (251)

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K customer concentration: Arrow Electronics, Microchip's largest distributor, accounted for 12% of net sales in fiscal 2026 (10% in fiscal 2025, 12% in fiscal 2024) and 14% of accounts receivable at March 31, 2026; no other distributor or direct customer exceeded 10%. Distributors were 47% of net sales in fiscal 2026 (45% in fiscal 2025). Microchip had approximately 101,000 customers; its ten largest direct customers were approximately 11% of total revenue, and two of the top ten direct customers are contract manufacturers.
quarterly_data.figure: Arrow Electronics 12% of FY2026 net sales (10% FY2025); distributors 47% (45%); ~101,000 customers; top ten direct customers ~11%

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K manufacturing and supply: in fiscal 2026 approximately 35% of sales came from products made in Microchip's own U.S. wafer fabs and approximately 65% from outside wafer foundries (64% in fiscal 2025), which supply all of its 300mm wafer requirements and some 200mm and 150mm specialty processes; third-party contractors performed approximately 33% of assembly and 31% of test requirements. Microchip holds long-term commitment contracts with certain third-party suppliers to secure wafer, assembly and test capacity; its purchase commitments, which primarily consist of agreements for the purchase of goods and services including wafer purchase obligations with its wafer foundries and manufacturing supply capacity reservation commitments, total $504.1 million, of which $344.0 million falls in fiscal 2027. Capital expenditures were $91.1 million in fiscal 2026 versus $126.0 million; investments in equipment and facilities over the next 12 months are expected at approximately $100.0 million, which management believes will support new products and bring in-house more of the outsourced assembly and test. The Fab 5 SiC and 8-inch expansion remains paused through fiscal 2027, and the Fab 2 (Tempe) closure was completed in May 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: ~65% of sales from outside foundries (64%); 33% assembly / 31% test outsourced; purchase commitments $504.1 million ($344.0 million in FY2027); capex $91.1 million ($126.0 million); next-12-month capex ~$100.0 million

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K long-term supply agreements: of $461.2 million of deferred revenue at March 31, 2026, $365.7 million is cash collected from customers under LTSAs, under which customers pay an upfront deposit and make minimum purchase commitments in exchange for assured supply over a contract period that typically ranges from three to five years; the deposit is returned if the customer meets its commitments and may be retained if not.
quarterly_data.figure: $365.7 million of LTSA deposits within $461.2 million deferred revenue
